feature.summary: Not shown to users. The server reserves an estimated cost before each image, settles it after, and a workspace spend cap can refuse the request. The monthly image quota is empty on every plan. No app shows an image price or a count of images left; only refusal messages point to Usage.

purpose.what_it_does: Would show what an image costs and how many generations remain. Today the server meters usage and enforces limits, and the apps show only the refusal text when a limit is hit. (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/managed-image-generation.ts:703-756; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/actions/mediaGenerationError.ts:7-8)
purpose.why_it_exists: Inference cost is a first-class design constraint and image generation is expensive (rate limit comment: expensive operation) (doc: AGENTS.md section 7; apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:384-388). Users would expect to know what a generation uses. The brief marks both items not applicable on every app. (brief S44.14, S44.15)
purpose.who_uses_it: Would be: paying users watching spend; workspace admins using spend caps.
problems_solved: Knowing when a limit will reset.
use_cases: See '8 images left today' for a free offer (not built).
Hit a spend cap and be told to see Usage (built as an error).

where_to_find_it: No cost or remaining count in image mode on Web, Desktop, Mobile or CLI (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6254-6460; AddToChatSheet.tsx:1003-1046; apps/cli/src/cloud/image.rs:236-258).

When a limit is hit: Mobile shows "You've reached your plan's usage limit for now. See Usage in Settings for when it resets." (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/actions/mediaGenerationError.ts:7-8). Web maps quota error codes to a 'view_usage' recovery action (apps/web/lib/hooks/useMediaGeneration.ts:208) and lists upgrade, subscribe, manage billing, top up actions (useMediaGeneration.ts:124-131).
screens_and_controls: None for cost or allowance. The free image offer is decided internally from a catalogue that carries remainingToday, but no display of it was found (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/freeQuotaCatalogue.ts:186-196).
journey: 2. If the plan, spend cap or provider quota refuses, a message appears.
3. Otherwise the image is made and nothing about cost or remaining count is shown.
feedback_and_outputs: Refusal errors: 403 plan_upgrade_required, 403 subscription_required, 402 or 429 insufficient_quota, spend-limit refusal from the compute gate (managed-image-generation.ts:118-132,159-170,196-211; route.ts:86-89).
CLI prints a summary of model, provider and settings but no cost (apps/cli/src/cloud/image.rs:236-258).
settings: Workspace spend cap is set elsewhere (managed-compute-gate); not part of image mode.

working: Spend cap is checked before any reservation (apps/web/app/api/media/image/generate/route.ts:86-89).

Cost is estimated per provider, quality and count, converted to a charge, and reserved with a lease that outlives all job attempts (image-generation-provider.ts:344-375; managed-image-generation.ts:703-756).
Failure, refusal, cancel and unsaved images release or settle at zero charge (image-job-executor.ts:137-160,192-232; media-image-generate.test.ts:1048,2014-2084).
Web and Mobile map quota refusals to messages and recovery actions (useMediaGeneration.ts:124-131,208; runImageGenerationTurn.ts:362-366).
Rate limit 10 requests per minute, fail closed (apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:384-388).
incomplete: Monthly image quota field imageQuotaPerMonth is null on the three plan entries inspected, so no per-plan image count is applied from it (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1292,1338,1389). An imageSyntheticTokenCost of 50,000 is also defined (model-catalog.ts:1293); how it is used was not traced.

The mobile response type has a cost_estimate field that the route never sets (apps/mobile/src/features/image/services/imagegen.ts:25; apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/managed-image-generation.ts:949-969).
disconnected_or_disabled: Limited free media offers carry a daily count (up to 10 images per UTC day, per docs) that decides whether an offer is shown, but the count itself is not shown (doc: docs/product/definition.md:342-347; freeQuotaCatalogue.ts:186-196).
not_available: Cost indication before or after generating: Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, Chrome.
Remaining-allowance display: Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, Chrome.

Every subscription capability connects to one AGI Subscription system covering entitlements, usage accounting, quotas and limits.

acceptance_criteria: A request refused for plan returns 403 plan_upgrade_required with current_plan and required_plans.
A request refused by the workspace spend cap is refused before any usage is reserved.
A refused or failed image leaves usage settled at zero charge for the account.
Today: no cost or remaining count is shown in image mode on any app.
If a display is added: it must come from the same subscription and usage source as the Usage screen, never a copy of plan numbers in the client (AGENTS.md section 4).
inferred: The brief's 'not applicable' likely records that no allowance exists to display (imageQuotaPerMonth is null) [inferred from model-catalog.ts:1292]; it may not mean the feature is out of scope.
Cost display must obey any product policy for Free users; none was found in the project docs I read [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Return the settled charge in the generate and status responses and show it on the image card and in the CLI summary.
[proposed] Show remaining free offers only if the product decision allows meters on the Free plan.
[proposed] Link the refusal message directly to the Usage screen on Web and Mobile.

steps.what_happens: The request passes the rate limit and the workspace spend cap check.
The server estimates cost and reserves it atomically against the plan; a refusal returns 402 or 429 insufficient_quota, or 503 billing_unavailable.
After the attempt, the reservation is finalized at the settled cost, or released at zero for failure, refusal or cancel.
The client shows a refusal message only; no figure is returned to display.

corrections.claim: Failure, refusal, cancel and unsaved images release or settle at zero charge
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The account is released. Failure and cancel go through settleFailure with actualCostMicrousd 0 (image-job-executor.ts:137-160). An unsaved image calls recordUndeliveredImageCost, which records the real provider cost as actualCostCents in the cost ledger with taskOutcome 'undelivered' (image-job-executor.ts:111-135, 783-799). The user is not charged, but the platform books a provider cost.
corrections.correction: Failed, cancelled and unsaved images release the reservation at zero charge to the account. For unsaved output the provider cost is still recorded as an undelivered cost in the ledger.

corrections.claim: imageQuotaPerMonth is null on the three plan entries inspected
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The null values are at model-catalog.ts:1292, 1338 and 1389 (the pro, max and enterprise entries). The free entry (line 1234) has no image fields at all, so the field is unset there rather than null. The field is optional (line 1103). imageSyntheticTokenCost is referenced only in the type, these three entries and tier-policies.test.ts:123, so it is not used in any runtime path.
corrections.correction: Pro, Max and Enterprise set imageQuotaPerMonth to null, and Free does not set it. imageSyntheticTokenCost (50,000) has no consumer outside a test. Section 7 should not say 'null on every plan'.

corrections.claim: A refusal returns 402 or 429 insufficient_quota, or 503 billing_unavailable (managed-image-generation.ts:118-132,703-767). The Runs-on column says the client refusal message is shown on 'device'.
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The citation 118-132 is not the quota refusal. Lines 118-132 hold managedUsageErrorResponse, which maps status 402 or 429 to type 'insufficient_quota' and anything else to 'invalid_request_error'. The 503 billing_unavailable fallback is at 757-766. The 402/429 status comes from ManagedUsageRequestError thrown by reserveManagedUsageRequest, and the page does not trace that. The 403 subscription_required, subscription gate and plan_upgrade_required checks sit at about lines 159-211. Also the 'device' row covers Web, which is a browser client.
corrections.correction: The 402 or 429 is raised by reserveManagedUsageRequest and mapped by managedUsageErrorResponse (118-132). Only a failure that is not a ManagedUsageRequestError becomes 503 billing_unavailable (757-766). Repoint the line citations.

corrections.claim: Image generation is a plan capability (Premium and above) (billing-catalog.ts:356)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: billing-catalog.ts:356 sets image_generation: PRO_TIERS. PRO_TIERS (line 341) is pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium and enterprise, so it includes the team tiers. The route also needs an active subscription (403 subscription_required) and passes evaluateManagedComputeSubscriptionAccess (managed-image-generation.ts:159-211). The page does not mention that Free users are refused by the managed route.
corrections.correction: Image generation needs an active subscription on pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium or enterprise. Other plans get 403 plan_upgrade_required with required_plans.

corrections.claim: Account: signed-in account; usage accounted per user and workspace
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The route needs a Clerk user (getClerkAuthUser), CSRF validation and an adult-eligibility age gate (buildAdultEligibilityGateResponse, gate 'media-image') before any cost gate. Reservation is keyed on userId, and the scoped organizationId and tenant check are also used. The page lists none of the CSRF or age-gate rules.
corrections.correction: Add that CSRF validation and an 18-and-over eligibility gate run before the rate limit result is used. The rate limit is applied first, then the age gate, then the managed compute gate, then org policy, then the spend cap.

corrections.claim: Retry after failure reuses the same reservation, so no double charge (managed-image-generation.ts:742-744)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: Lines 742-744 are only a comment: the durable job holds one reservation across every attempt, so the lease must outlive the schedule. That supports reuse within one job (the job-level retry in image-job-executor). It does not show that a client-initiated retry reuses the reservation. recordUndeliveredImageCost says 'a retry pays the provider again' (image-job-executor.ts:109-110), so the provider is charged per attempt even though the account is not.
corrections.correction: One durable job holds one reservation across its automatic attempts, so the account is not charged twice. The provider cost is incurred again per attempt, and undelivered attempts are recorded as undelivered cost.

corrections.claim: Web maps quota error codes to a 'view_usage' recovery action (useMediaGeneration.ts:208) and lists upgrade, subscribe, manage billing, top up (124-131)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: Lines 124-131 hold the type MediaPaywallRecoveryAction and the PAYWALL_ERROR_RECOVERY map: insufficient_credits to upgrade, plan_upgrade_required to upgrade, subscription_required to subscribe, subscription_inactive to manage_billing. top_up appears only in the type, in no map entry. view_usage is returned at line 208 via classifyManagedQuotaErrorCode. A bare status 402 also maps to 'upgrade' (about line 210).
corrections.correction: top_up is a declared action but nothing in this mapping returns it. A 402 with no recognised code falls back to 'upgrade'.

missing_facts: The image route runs an adult-eligibility (age) gate and CSRF validation before the cost gates, and the page's rules table omits both (apps/web/app/api/media/image/generate/route.ts:34-52).
Provider cost is recorded for undelivered images and charged again per attempt, even though the account is released (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/image-job-executor.ts:109-135,783-799).

The managed route needs an active subscription (403 subscription_required) and passes evaluateManagedComputeSubscriptionAccess before any plan check, so a Free account is refused here. The page does not say how the limited free image offer reaches this route (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/managed-image-generation.ts:159-211).
